newsitem.title: FRANCE: Cie Bancaire 12-yr 2-bln Ffr bond seen next week.
newsitem.headline: Cie Bancaire 12-yr 2-bln Ffr bond seen next week.

text.p: Compagnie Bancaire was expected to issue around two billion francs of 12-year French franc bonds next week, a source close to the syndicate teams said on Friday.
The market was also expecting French insurer AGF to raise some four billion francs, but it was not clear what kind of instrument it would use, traders said.

AGF declined to comment on a report in Friday's edition of the financial daily Les Echos which said the operation could be an "innovative" instrument. The article also said the issue would be led by Goldman Sachs.
Some traders said the issue might be an instrument similar to subordinated perpetual notes. No other issuers in francs next week were expected at the moment.

Current speculation that French President Jacques Chirac may dissolve parliament and call snap elections could prompt some potential borrowers in francs to shelve their projects for now, bankers said.

Brazil was due to hold investor presentations in France next week ahead of its five-year franc issue, expected by the end of April. The franc issue will be a so-called parallel bond, with the same maturity date and coupon as two other issues due in guilders and schillings.
The franc issue will be equivalent to about $200 million and will be fungible with the other two bonds after the introduction of a single currency.
